summary_html: Agency **files a court petition** to open a **dependency** (or similar) case. Federal funding frameworks (IV-E/ASFA) link court oversight, reasonable-efforts findings, and permanency timelines to downstream actions.
authority_html:
- **ASFA / SSA Title IV-E** — court findings; timelines; permanency planning  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal review of court/agency performance measures

primary_citations.citation_text: Maryland - Md. Code, Family Law Article §§ 5-701 et seq. (Child Abuse and Neglect; definitions at § 5-701, mandatory reporting at §§ 5-704 and 5-705, investigation at § 5-706, appeal of findings at § 5-706.1)
Maryland - Courts & Judicial Proc. § 3-801 et seq. (CINA—Child in Need of Assistance proceedings)

provisions_triggered.name: Due Process / Law of the Land

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.citation: No. 1267, Sept. Term 2020 (Md. Ct. Spec. App. July 29, 2021)
key_cases.court: Court of Special Appeals of Maryland
key_cases.holding: The court vacated a CINA adjudication and disposition, holding that at a contested adjudicatory hearing the department must introduce evidence complying with the Maryland Rules, and that findings resting solely on attorney proffers and an unadmitted report are clearly erroneous.
key_cases.relevance: It defines what the department must actually prove, and how, once it files a CINA petition that the parent contests.
key_cases.quote: the court's findings of fact at the contested adjudicatory hearing were clearly erroneous because they were based solely on proffers from counsel and the unadmitted Report

key_cases.holding: The Court held that a juvenile court may award custody under CJP § 3-819(e) only after sustaining the petition against one parent and finding the other able and willing to care for the child, that the best-interest standard governs the exercise of that discretion, and that the parent must be allowed an evidentiary hearing on material disputes.
key_cases.relevance: It defines the findings that must support a CINA petition before the court may reallocate custody instead of adjudicating the child CINA.
key_cases.quote: If those prerequisites are established, the best interest of the child is the standard that applies to the court's decision whether and, if so, how to exercise that discretion

key_cases.case_name: Horridge v. St. Mary's County Department of Social Services
key_cases.holding: Reversing dismissal of a wrongful-death complaint, the Court held that FL § 5-706 and its regulations create a mandatory duty owed to the identified child named in an abuse report, so the public duty doctrine does not bar a negligence action against the department and its caseworkers.
key_cases.relevance: It notes the department's obligation to petition the juvenile court when the child's protection requires it.
key_cases.quote: This is not an obligation that runs to everyone in general and no one in particular. It runs to an identified or identifiable child or discrete group of children.

key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed a CINA adjudication entered on stipulated facts, holding that a parent's right to a contested CINA adjudicatory hearing is not among the rights requiring a personal, knowing, intelligent and voluntary waiver, and that counsel's concurrence in the stipulated facts in the petition waived it.
key_cases.relevance: It governs what happens procedurally once a department files a CINA petition, and in particular the effect of a parent's counsel agreeing to the facts alleged in it.
key_cases.quote: Ms. H.'s waiver of a contested CINA adjudicatory hearing was sufficient when her attorney concurred with the stipulated facts.

timeline_requirements.deadline: 10 days to the extent possible; if not completed within 30 days, within 60 days
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Receipt of the first notice of the suspected abuse or neglect
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in Md. Code, Fam. Law § 5-706
